memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Circumcise your hearts, therefore, and do not be stiff-necked any longer. - Deut 10:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is one of the most striking commands in the whole book. Circumcision was the physical sign of belonging to God's covenant people. But here Moses says something deeper: "Circumcise your hearts." He is calling for an inward reality, not just an outward mark. God was never satisfied with external religion alone. He wanted hearts that were truly His — softened, surrendered, and set apart to Him. Then he adds, "do not be stiff-necked any longer" — stop the stubborn resistance.

This gets to the heart of true faith. It is entirely possible to bear all the outward signs of religion — attending services, knowing the right words, following the rituals — while the heart remains hard and unsurrendered. God looks past the externals to the inner person. What He desires is not merely religious performance but a transformed heart that loves and follows Him from within.

The wonderful truth is that God does not just command this — He promises to do it. Later in Deuteronomy, God says He Himself will "circumcise your hearts... so that you may love him" (Deut 30:6). And the New Testament reveals this is fulfilled in Christ: true circumcision "is circumcision of the heart, by the Spirit" (Rom 2:29). What we cannot do for ourselves — soften and transform our own hearts — God does through His Spirit. Our part is to stop resisting, to surrender, to say yes to the work He wants to do within us. Ask God today to circumcise your heart, to remove all stubbornness, and to make you truly His from the inside out.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is my faith mainly external, or has God transformed my heart within?
- Where am I being "stiff-necked" — stubbornly resisting God?
- Will I surrender and ask God to soften and transform my heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You desire not just outward religion but a transformed heart. Circumcise my heart by Your Spirit, remove every trace of stubbornness, and make me truly Yours from the inside out. I stop resisting, and surrender to Your work in me. Amen.
